html:
The second Libyan civil war was fought from 2014 to 2020 between rival governments in the west, based in Tripoli, and the east, where General Khalifa Haftar built up his Libyan National Army.

After the revolution of 2011, elections in 2014 produced two parliaments. Militias lined up behind each. The Islamic State held Sirte for a time in 2015 and 2016. In 2019 Haftar attacked Tripoli, backed by the UAE, Egypt and Russian mercenaries, while Turkey sent drones and troops to save the Tripoli government.

A ceasefire in October 2020 ended the main fighting, but Libya stays divided. In the chaos the country became the main route for migrants trying to reach Europe. See also Gaddafi.
sum: The second Libyan civil war was fought from 2014 to 2020 between rival governments in the west, based in Tripoli, and the east, where General Khalifa Haftar built up his Libyan National Army.
